entries.title: Manipuri at a glance
body: Manipuri, also called Meeteilon or Meitei, is the official language of the state of Manipur in north-east India and one of India's 22 scheduled languages. It has about 1.8 million first-language speakers and is a common language among many communities in Manipur.
It is a Sino-Tibetan language. The verb comes last, small endings mark the subject, object and place, and it is tonal, with two tones.

entries.title: Meetei Mayek
body: Meetei Mayek is the traditional script of Manipuri. It was replaced by the Bengali script for about two centuries and was brought back in the 1970s and 1980s; it is now taught in schools and used on signs alongside Bengali script.

Its first 18 letters are named after parts of the human body: ꯀ (kok) is the head, ꯁ (sam) the hair, ꯂ (lai) the forehead, ꯃ (mit) the eye, ꯄ (pa) the eyelash, ꯅ (na) the ear. Like other Brahmi-family scripts each consonant carries a vowel, and vowel signs change it. Special final letters (lonsum) write a consonant at the end of a syllable, as in ꯆꯥꯛ, chak.

entries.title: Ima Keithel
body: Ima Keithel (ꯏꯃꯥ ꯀꯩꯊꯦꯜ), “mothers' market”, in Imphal is a market run entirely by women, with several thousand stall holders. It has existed for centuries and is often called the largest market of its kind.
Manipur is also known as a home of modern polo, played there as sagol kangjei, and of the Manipuri classical dance, one of India's classical dance forms.
